newsitem.title: UK: FX IN EUROPE: DLR SIDELINED, STERLING STUMBLES.
newsitem.headline: FX IN EUROPE: DLR SIDELINED, STERLING STUMBLES.

text.p: The dollar weakened against the mark but stayed sidelined as sterling tumbled amid expectations that UK interest rates have peaked for now, traders said.

Sterling fell back below the psychologically important 3.00 mark level after the Bank of England raised interest rates by a quarter point to 7.00 percent and said their current level was consistent with the government's 2.5 percent inflation target. "The BOE have achieved their objective of tightening monetary policy and bringing sterling down at the same time," said Daiwa Europe senior economist Sally Wilkinson.

Sterling's precipitous decline followed a sharp sell-off on Wednesday amid fund selling as doubts about the interest rate horizon grabbed hold of the market. The UK currency has now fallen over nine pfennigs from this week's high at 3.0633 and is down nearly five cents from a peak of $1.6345.

"The market is viewing today's hike as the limit for interest rates for the time being, and that served as a good reason to take profits," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London. "I think the market is getting too cautious about rates but sterling is vulnerable."

At 1530 GMT the pound was at 2.9712/22 marks, up from a low at 2.9640 but down from 3.0130 in late European trading on Wednesday. Against the dollar it stood at 1.5848/56 from a low of 1.5780 and Wednesday's European close at $1.6038.
Dollar/mark was at 1.8723/33 from 1.8808 late on Wednesday, while against the yen the dollar was at 118.40/50 from 118.53.

Analysts said the pound had more downside potential against the dollar than the mark because of more favourable U.S. fundamentals. The robust economic background in the U.S. is likely to keep firing the dollar and many traders still expect a stab at the 1.90 mark barrier.

A dampener for dollar bulls however is speculation that the Bundesbank will allow money market rates to drift higher if the mark slides beyond the near-eight year low it has been lingering at against the U.S. currency.

Analysts also pointed to weekly foreign exchange reserve data from the Bundesbank which indicated discrete selling of dollars by the German central bank. Reserves fell sharply by 1.2 billion marks in the seven days to July 23.
"It sends a signal that it's not just rhetoric when the Bundesbank expresses concern about the mark even though it has had little effect on the dollar rally," said Meggyesi.
Dollar/yen was dampened by persistent concern about potential trade tensions between the U.S. and Japan.

Comments made by U.S. trade representative Charlene Barshefsky on Wednesday fanned such concern and triggered demand for yen in Asia. She said Japan could not rely too much on exports to promote growth. But demand from U.S. funds below 118 yen pushed the dollar off lows, traders said.

The mark jumped against the Finnish markka after finance minister Sauli Niinisto said the currency's central rate in the European exchange rate mechanism would be the right level at which to enter European monetary union.

His comment slammed the markka, whose ERM central parity is 3.0400 to the mark, down to a session low of 2.9915 compared with 2.9778 in late European trading on Wednesday. It was at 2.9905/35 in late trade here.

The Irish punt, which is the strongest currency against the mark in the ERM grid after the markka, also fell, mainly due to the slide in sterling. The punt fell as low as 2.6753 marks, compared with 2.6975 late Wednesday.
The mark's other crosses ignored sterling's weakness and were mostly steady.
